claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known model-card weakness, because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the rollout starts at 6% with rollback and monitoring.
specific_concerns: The policy text requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance covering the exposure; the available summary says neither condition is met.
The affected small-business onboarding segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate does not exclude the affected segment.
The draft risk acceptance is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment.
Rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring are described in the policy as insufficient to remove disclosure duties when exposure remains.
unsupported_claims: That the certification is policy-compliant on the current record.
That rollout controls and monitoring are enough to mitigate the material model-card weakness while the affected segment remains exposed.
That the decision is merely a caveated but compliant certification rather than an unresolved policy failure.
evidence_requests: Provide a reviewed and approved risk acceptance that explicitly covers the small-business onboarding exposure and explains why continued exposure is acceptable.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout cohort excludes the affected small-business onboarding use case if that is the intended basis for compliance.
Provide the actual model-card disclosure or equivalent documentation showing how the known weakness is disclosed for the exposed segment.
Provide the governing approval record tying the certification decision to one of the policy-allowed predicates.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if admissible evidence shows the affected use case is excluded from rollout, or approved risk acceptance explicitly covers the continued exposure.

Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollback capability, and monitoring can support operational readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy predicate.
Known limiting facts that remain unresolved in the record weigh against compliance rather than merely against confidence.
